findings.quote: `public.redeem_join_code(code text, message text default null) returns jsonb` — … find `join_codes` by `code = normalized::extensions.citext`
findings.problem: plpgsql's default `variable_conflict = error` makes `where code = …` fail at runtime with "column reference \"code\" is ambiguous" because the parameter `code` shadows `join_codes.code`. The same trap exists in `approve_join_request(request_id, person_id, note)` (`set person_id = coalesce(person_id, …)`), `create_join_code(… label, auto_approve, expires_at, max_uses)` and `reject_join_request(…, note)`. The parameter names must stay (1.7a's `rpc.ts` passes keys equal to the SQL parameter names), so the bodies need qualification.
findings.fix: Add to Build 1 (5) a rule: "Alias every table (`from public.join_codes jc`, `public.join_requests r`) and qualify every column (`jc.code`, `r.person_id`); refer to a shadowed parameter by function name (`redeem_join_code.code`, `approve_join_request.person_id`). Never rely on `#variable_conflict use_column`." Add an assertion to Build 3: each RPC is called once with every parameter supplied so an ambiguity error would surface in `11_join_codes.sql`.

findings.quote: If `check-rerunnable.sh` or `08_rerunnable.sql` assumes a single migration file, generalise it minimally and record the change.

Keep the psql-only comment 1.4a wrote." Add to Verify: `bash scripts/db/test.sh --only 08_rerunnable` → PASS.

findings.quote: parameterised by psql variables with defaults (`\set` guarded by `\if`): `:persons_a` 5000, `:persons_b` 2000, `:budget_ms` 250 … using a `do $$` block … Assertions: every `ms <= :budget_ms`
findings.problem: psql does not interpolate `:var` inside quoted literals, including dollar-quoted `do $$ … $$` bodies, so `:budget_ms`, `:persons_a`, `:orgA` are passed to the server verbatim and the block fails to parse (or the assertion never sees the budget). The runner's `-v budget_ms=` therefore cannot reach the assertion as written.
findings.fix: Add to Build 1: "psql variables are invisible inside `do $$` bodies: right after the `\set` defaults run `select set_config('perf.budget_ms', :'budget_ms', true), set_config('perf.persons_a', :'persons_a', true), set_config('perf.persons_b', :'persons_b', true);` and read them inside plpgsql with `current_setting('perf.budget_ms')::numeric`; capture generated org ids the same way (`select set_config('perf.org_a', id::text, true)`) or with `\gset` outside the block." Keep `PERF_BUDGET_MS=1` in Verify as the proof the assertion is live.
